code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Periodic preventive visit; no new complaints. [S]

Mr. Turing is a 41-year-old mathematician who comes for his periodic preventive visit two weeks after his six-month review. He completed the health risk assessment before the visit. His ankle recovered within three weeks of the August visit; he took ibuprofen for four days and is back to about 40 km a week. His depression is in remission on bupropion XL 150 mg with monthly psychotherapy sessions, and his testosterone has been normal since August. The breast tissue is no longer tender. He has had no suicidal thoughts. He has not had HIV or STI testing since moving here and would like it today. He has had one new male partner in the past three months and uses condoms most of the time. [S]

Periodic preventive visit, age 41. Health risk assessment reviewed and a written prevention plan given. Ten-year cardiovascular risk is under 2 percent by the pooled cohort equations, so a statin is not recommended. Sexual health care offered as routine adult care. [S]
HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B and C serology, and urine, pharyngeal, and rectal gonorrhea and chlamydia tests drawn today with his consent; he will be told the results by secure message.
PrEP explained: with one partner, condoms most of the time, and no recent STI he does not now meet the indications, and he will tell us if that changes; PrEP is available here whenever it is right for him.
Next preventive visit in one year.

Major depressive disorder, single episode, in remission (F32.1). PHQ-9 3, in remission on bupropion with psychotherapy. Safety reviewed: no suicidal thoughts, intent, or plan; protective factors stronger than at intake. [S]
Continue bupropion XL 150 mg for at least six to nine months after remission, then decide together whether to taper.
Collaborative safety plan reviewed and unchanged, with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and the clinic number.

Residual gynecomastia, improving (N62). Smaller and non-tender, six months after the estrogen stopped. [S]
Watchful waiting; a plastic surgery opinion if it persists about twelve months after the estrogen stopped and he wants it removed.

Follow-up: Results by secure message within a week. COVID-19 vaccine at a pharmacy. Hepatitis A and HPV vaccine decisions at the next visit. Depression review in about two months. Next preventive visit in one year. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with his consent. He named a health care agent, a close friend, and completed a health care proxy form; the agent is recorded in the chart and is not named here. He said that what matters most to him is being able to think and work, and that no treatment should ever be given to him without his own agreement or, if he cannot speak, his agent's. He wants full treatment for reversible illness. He asked that his records, including his sexual orientation and the history of the estrogen he was given, be shared only with clinicians treating him. The plan will be revisited yearly. [S]
